biografia: Lt. Leon Freeman is a relatively inexperienced Mechwarrior, with only a few years of 'Merc experience under his belt. After his lancemates were wiped out while protecting Sebastian Spears' dig site, he found himself without a company. When Commander Mason offered him employment, Freeman leapt at the chance.

Born on Randar in 2992, Dimitri Shenzeng comes from a long line of Mechwarriors who proudly served the Capellan Confederation. His allegiances began to shift however, when he was rescued by Captain Mason after he had been captured by a band of pirates. Dimitri's deep sense of honor compelled him to declare a life debt to Commander Mason. He has served dutifully under Mason ever since.

Cornelius Kaffenberger III used to be a part of Nik’s Cavaliers before striking out for what he saw as greener pastures.  He has since rejoined the Cavaliers and not much is known about his time away but he claims to have travelled all over the Inner Sphere, though never anywhere nice, and that he has “seen some [censored] ya wouldn’t believe.”  And now the only name he responds to is his callsign, Goblin.  His boasts include defeating a company of enemy 'Mechs by himself, taking out an assault 'Mech in one shot, and stealing a pie from the Bounty Hunter.

A former informant for The Bounty Hunter and the sole survivor of a BattleMech mercenary unit that went by Akai-Hebi, or "The Red Snakes," the individual that only goes by his MechWarrior call sign of Raptor is a highly talented MechWarrior suffering from a severe case of survivor's guilt over the death of his former colleagues. While he has never elaborated on the specifics on the incident that saw his former unit wiped out, rumor has it that his extracurricular activities with the Bounty Hunter might have played a part in it.
Grew up with one dream: to be a pilot for DCMS and fend off any enemies that may threaten his homeland.
Grew up with a rebellious streak, unwilling to conform to her family's wishes for her future, eventually becoming a pilot for Merc units and never looked back.
While he may find peace in the fields of his family farm, his true love is piloting a ‘Mech and engaging in fierce combat.

Ash didn’t choose the mercenary life—it was inked into his birth certificate. The son of Elias Delmore, a long-time recruiter on Galatea known for signing greenbloods to bad contracts, Ash grew up behind the scenes of the mercenary trade. While other kids played with toys, Ash listened to negotiation tactics, learned to read contracts, and watched washed-up veterans barter away their futures for one more shot at glory.
His father never intended for him to pilot a ’Mech—he wanted a businessman, not a soldier. But Ash had other plans.
Now a competent and clever medium ’Mech pilot, Ash mixes tactical caution with sharp battlefield instincts—and never signs anything without reading the fine print.

Barrett Nolan was born in New Starburg, a gleaming industrial city on the Lyran world of Rodigo, and son to a member of the New Starburg Mechanized Cavalry—a planetary militia regiment that that defended the soil when called upon.

His father, Colonel Tomas Nolan, served the NSMC with pride, and expected his son to do the same. Barrett was raised on drill fields, taught honor, protocol, and the legacy of duty. And for a while, he walked that path—until he saw what that “duty” actually meant: taking orders tied to politics, not principle. Fighting battles not for justice, but for obligation. Being handed a lance assignment, not choosing a cause.
That did not sit well with him. Barrett’s fiery temper and hunger for battle meant he would put his services up for sale and be able to head into battle when the price and cause are right to him.

Jacob grew up in the Lovinac system near the Gregor Mines – where his older brother Derek taught him a relentless work ethic that he carried over in into the cockpit of a ‘Mech. For decades Lovinac housed a secret stockpile of ‘Mechs that remained hidden until Hendrick Grimm unearthed them in the 3040s.

But growing up, Jacob was fortunate enough to stumble upon a ‘Mech being used for field testing before it was hidden, a moment that inspired awe and wonder within Jake that carried him through his formative years until he was finally able to get inside of a cockpit himself.

After that day, Jake could never settle for a simple life working in the mines, hearing whispers of battles and conflicts that were shaping the destiny of the Inner Sphere, MechWarriors washing blood from their hands, while has busy scrubbing dirt from his.Jake always brings his work boots to any contract he signs, always willing to outwork his opponent no matter what, or how long it takes.

Lance Gabel is uncertain of his true parentage, having been raised in pirate’s den inside the Oberon Confederation, a periphery nation located on the coreward rim of the Lyran Commonwealth near The Draconis Combine.Thought to be the bastard son of a pirate, Lance was raised among cutthroats and scavengers, he was taught to treat battle as brutality, not discipline. He piloted his first ’Mech during a raid on a mining colony—and hated every second of it.

Despite his skill, Lance never had the taste for terror. Where others saw opportunity in chaos, he saw waste. Over the years, he became known for ending fights quickly and with minimal damage—sometimes letting targets go entirely. It didn’t take long for that to earn him the wrong kind of attention.Branded a traitor and left for dead after refusing to execute prisoners on a raid, Lance severed his pirate affiliations. He spent months in the shadows before resurfacing with a new identity as a merc for hire.

Now, Lance fights for mercenary companies that value precision over carnage. Though he rarely speaks of his past, his quiet demeanour and code of restraint tell you all you need to know—this is a man trying to turn sin into service.

Lyana Moore spent her early years in the Alleghe System, a quiet, rural frontier known for its massive AG Centers—facilities responsible for supplying food across large swathes of the region. She grew up in the shadow of domes and silos, tending hydroponic gardens and learning patience, care, and the quiet rhythm of life rooted in the soil.That ended in fire.An explosion at one of the AG centers—suspected sabotage, though no one ever claimed responsibility—killed dozens, including both of her parents. At age twelve, Lyana was pulled from the only home she’d ever known and sent to live with relatives in a remote, frosty part of the system. There, she met the man who would shape her future: her great-grandfather, Cormac Moore, a grizzled, retired mercenary who’d fought and survived many conflicts across the Inner Sphere.

Cormac saw the loss in Lyana’s eyes, and instead of trying to soothe it, he taught her to forge it into resolve. Over years of simulator training, ’Mech maintenance, and harsh survival drills, Lyana learned the art of war—not out of bloodlust, but to ensure she’d never be powerless again.

Now a full-fledged mercenary in her own right, Lyana pilots her ’Mech with eerie calm and discipline. Still carrying a small vial of Alleghe soil in her cockpit, Lyana never forgets the flames that forged her destiny as a MechWarrior.

Morgan Trensky wasn’t born into nobility—but he may as well have been made for it.Raised during the Rise of Rasalhague, Morgan grew up under constant threat of violence. He enlisted with a local militia when they would take him, then later began putting up his services to the highest bidder—quickly proving himself as a battlefield anchor: cool under fire, immovable, and brutally efficient when protecting assets.

His reputation as an unbreakable shield reached the ears of Prince Haakon Magnusson himself. Impressed by his exploits and prowess on the battlefield, Magnusson requested him to serve on his security detail.
Though he remained technically a mercenary, his loyalty to the FRR —and to Magnusson—never wavered.

Born near the hustle and bustle of Galatea’s capital city Nick grew up in the shadow of the new MechWarrior games developed on Galatea, much more brutal and uncivilized than the ones held on Solaris VII.

Lured by the glory, and the prospect of piloting a ‘Mech from a legendary fallen foe, Nick entered the games as soon as possible, piloting a scavenged ‘Mech he won off of a member of a Galatea street gang. Nick’s skills caught the eye of promoters and recruiters alike. Nick carved out a reputation for stubborn, punishing brawls. While never the flashiest pilot, he was relentless—winning crowd respect for his ability to turn scrapheap machines into war trophies.

Nick’s exploits also inspired his younger step-sister Rachel, who followed him into the arena. Eventually the two began drawing contract offers from mercenary outfits. The two MechWarriors would often refuse to fight apart, fighting side by side when possible.

Rachel Laird grew up in the shadow of her older and fellow merc step-brother Nick’s arena fame, but quickly made a name of her own. Agile, aggressive, and terrifyingly precise, she specialized in light ’Mech duels and was notorious for humiliating slower, bulkier opponents in the circuits.
Unlike Nick, Rachel didn’t crave the spotlight—she thrived on making others chase ghosts. Her tactical instincts and flair for unpredictability made her the perfect MechWarrior in the arena.
When the offers came to join real mercenary outfits, Rachel made every effort to sign up for jobs that would allow her to fight alongside her brother, whenever possible.

Sam Hagel was raised on Almunge, a world within the Draconis Combine where discipline and tradition ran as deep as the snowdrifts. Sam was an adopted son and resided with his adopted family in a town steeped in bushido and loyal to the Dragon, Sam trained under retired DCMS instructors, absorbing the values of honor, obedience, and martial precision from a young age.Though he respected the way of the samurai, he grew uneasy with the Combine’s rigid hierarchy and the disdain it held for mercenaries. To Hagel, true honor wasn’t in blind obedience, but in choosing your battles—and why you fought them.

Eventually, he left Almunge under heavy scrutiny. Branded a dishonorable outcast by some, a rogue idealist by others, he instead carved out a name as an independent contract—fighting with a blend of Combine precision and personal conviction.
Now a respected mercenary, Sam Hagel is known for his clean, efficient combat style and unwavering battlefield ethics. He avoids contracts built on exploitation and insists on fighting on his terms.

Sasha is a MechWarrior through and through. She grew up in the icy tundra of Caldrith, a Northen city located in Jarret. Her older sister Kira was a merc who took a job to root out a band of savage pirates and never came home – at least not in one piece.

Sasha’s curiosity about Kira’s fate eventually led her to a cockpit of a ‘Mech, but only after years of the cold darkness of her surroundings, and the visuals of her sister’s grisly fate fueled her desire to follow in her sister’s footsteps and fight against injustice as she saw fit.

Sasha’s ferocity and swiftness on the battlefield make her a formidable opponent for anyone who faces her, but the anger and sadness about her sister’s fate live within her and can sometimes send her into an emotional state that leaves her vulnerable.No matter what job she signs up for, Sasha tackles with a cold resolve that makes her a valuable asset for any merc outfit.

Since the Succession Wars, the Ryders have been a family attempting to restore their good name through loyal service to the Archon after failing to secede from the Lyran Commonwealth. But that is not a life that suited Valten. Seeing many of his family members fight and die at the whims of House Steiner, he instead chose to walk the life of a mercenary. Hiring out his talents to whoever would have them. While Valten is an exceptional MechWarrior, he is also a high-stakes gambler. Who has, on more than one occasion, racked up a large amount of debt through increasingly shadier underworld connections. Despite making a name for himself as one of the members of Adam Steiner’s famed “Somerset Strikers.”
